chemistries.title: Everyday power
chemistries.desc: The common single-use cell. Reliable, widely available and good at holding charge in storage.

chemistries.title: Rechargeable workhorse
chemistries.desc: Nickel-metal hydride cells can be recharged hundreds of times and suit regularly used devices.

chemistries.title: High energy density
chemistries.desc: Lightweight, high-capacity and rechargeable — the technology behind most modern electronics and larger storage systems.

sizes.use: The most common size — torches, remotes, toys, wireless peripherals and countless everyday devices.
Smaller devices where space is limited — slim remotes, small torches and electronic accessories.
Medium-drain devices needing more capacity, such as larger torches and portable radios.
High-drain, longer-running devices such as large flashlights and some industrial equipment.
Smoke alarms, detectors and specialist electronic equipment requiring a higher voltage.

recycle.title: Keep out of general waste
recycle.desc: Batteries should never go in your normal bin — many retailers and recycling points accept them free of charge.

recycle.title: Store safely before recycling
recycle.desc: Keep used batteries dry and, for lithium cells, tape the terminals to prevent short circuits before disposal.

recycle.title: Recover valuable materials
recycle.desc: Recycling recovers metals and reduces the environmental impact of battery production and disposal.
